data.title: The Coca-Cola Company Names David Elkins as Incoming Chief Financial Officer :: The Coca-Cola Company (KO)
data.summary: The Coca-Cola Company Names David Elkins as Incoming Chief Financial Officer Elkins to Succeed John Murphy, Who Will Continue to Serve as President of the Company ATLANTA--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- The Coca-Cola Company today announced that David Elkins, a finance leader with extensive experience across global pharmaceuticals and consumer products companies, will become executive vice president and chief financial officer of Coca-Cola April 2, 2027, succeeding John Murphy. We’re constantly transforming our portfolio, from reducing sugar in our drinks to bringing innovative new products to market. We seek to positively impact people’s lives, communities and the planet through water replenishment, packaging recycling, sustainable sourcing practices and carbon emissions reductions across [...] Murphy, 64, intends to retire in 2027, with timing determined later to allow for a smooth and orderly leadership transition for the CFO role. Murphy, who has been CFO since 2019, has been working with company leadership for some time to prepare for the succession process. Murphy will continue to serve as president, focusing on key enterprise priorities in 2027, in addition to the CFO transition. As CFO, Elkins’ oversight will include finance, global strategy and Enterprise Services.

data.title: Coca-Cola Company names new executive vice president, CFO
data.summary: ATLANTA — The Atlanta-based Coca-Cola Company announced it will have a new executive vice president and chief financial starting in April. David Elkins, who currently serves as executive vice president and CFO of Bristol Myers Squibb, will succeed John Murphy upon his retirement. Elkins takes the role officially on April 2, 2027. data.title: Coca-Cola ditched AI for its new holiday ad - Fast Company
data.summary: After two years of AI-generated holiday ads that spawned plenty of real-world backlash, Coca-Cola went live-action for its latest holiday campaign. Coca-Cola’s new spot “Enjoy Joy” shows real human actors as friends and family engaged in fall and winter activities, like playing football and having a turkey dinner. It ends with the word Enjoy written in its new tall, serifed typeface. [...] Coca-Cola was an early adopter to AI marketing, offering an online, AI-generated holiday card maker in 2023. It followed that up with its AI-generated remakes of “Holidays Are Coming” in 2024. Despite online criticism, it released yet another AI-generated ad last year that showed AI-generated snowscapes, winter creatures, and localized elements for geo-specific media buys, like a “Welcome to Boston” billboard in Boston. [...] Still, the company says viewers shouldn’t read into the choice too much. “This does not signal a broader shift, as Coca-Cola continues to explore different creative approaches and emerging technologies to bring its storytelling to life,” says Madison Chandler, a spokesperson for the company. “Human storytellers remain at the center of the creative process, with AI serving as a tool to support and enhance creative expression where appropriate.”
